Block worlds

13 calls on gfx, generated from the firmware. Every one exists on the device exactly as written here.

The voxel engine (engine v17). A byte-per-cell grid in PSRAM, remeshed per chunk and rasterised in one call.

gfx.vblock

gfx.vblock(id, top, side, bottom)

Palette indices per face. The renderer adds the lighting tier (gfx.mcam{tier=}) per face direction, so give it the BASE colour and let the tiers live at +tier / +2*tier as everywhere else.

#argument
1idrequired
2toprequired
3sideoptional, default same as top
4bottomoptional, default same as side

gfx.vbox

gfx.vbox(x, y, z, sx, sy, sz, block)

Draw one axis-aligned box this frame, ordered against the world. This is how a third-person character (or, later, a mob) exists: it cannot be a grid cell because it moves, and it cannot be a gfx.mesh because the voxel pass owns the span buffer and keeps no depth buffer for a later pass to test against. (x,y) is the centre, z the base.

#argument
1xrequired
2yrequired
3zrequired
4sxrequired
5syrequired
6szrequired
7blockrequired

gfx.vdraw

gfx.vdraw() -> quads drawn

Remeshes dirty chunks, then rasterises the whole world in ONE call through the span buffer: near-to-far, memset only what is still uncovered. Uses the gfx.mcam camera. No depth buffer is touched, so anything drawn after this must painter-order itself.

gfx.vfill

gfx.vfill(x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, block)

Inclusive box. Worldgen goes through here: a Lua triple loop over even a small world blows the per-callback instruction budget long before it finishes.

#argument
1x0required
2y0required
3z0required
4x1required
5y1required
6z1required
7blockrequired

gfx.vget

gfx.vget(x,y,z) -> block

The block id at one cell, 0 for air. Reading outside the world is 0 too rather than an error, so collision code can probe freely at the edges without bounds-checking first.

#argument
1xrequired
2yrequired
3zrequired

gfx.vload

gfx.vload(name) -> bool

engine v17

Persist the whole block world (engine v17). Names are [a-z0-9_]. It goes beside the app's documents (not in the app directory, which an update replaces), so a child's world survives a reinstall. The grid run-length-encodes itself in C: 368,640 cells is three orders of magnitude past the 4KB document cap and far past what Lua could walk on device.

#argument
1namerequired

gfx.vlod

gfx.vlod(dist)

How far out gfx.vpattern textures still draw (default 40 blocks). A textured span runs a per-pixel loop where a flat one is a memset, so this is the app's dial between how far the texture reads and how much of the frame the far field costs. 0 = texture everything.

#argument
1distrequired

gfx.vpattern

gfx.vpattern(id, accent, mask)

A 4x4 texture for one block type, the SAME on all six faces so a block is recognisable from any angle. mask is 16 bits read row-major (bit 0 = top-left); a set bit draws accent instead of the face colour. Both take the lighting tier, so a patterned block shades like a flat one. Omit it (or pass mask 0) and the block fills at memset speed.

#argument
1idrequired
2accentrequired
3maskrequired

gfx.vray

gfx.vray(x,y,z, dx,dy,dz [, maxd]) -> hx,hy,hz, px,py,pz | nil

The first solid cell along the ray and the empty cell just before it (break here, place there). This is the crosshair.

#argument
1xrequired
2yrequired
3zrequired
4dxrequired
5dyrequired
6dzrequired
7maxdoptional, default 8

gfx.vsave

gfx.vsave(name) -> bool

engine v17

Persist the whole block world (engine v17). Names are [a-z0-9_]. It goes beside the app's documents (not in the app directory, which an update replaces), so a child's world survives a reinstall. The grid run-length-encodes itself in C: 368,640 cells is three orders of magnitude past the 4KB document cap and far past what Lua could walk on device.

#argument
1namerequired

gfx.vset

gfx.vset(x,y,z,block)

0 = air. Marks the chunk (and any neighbour whose boundary faces change) for remesh; the next gfx.vdraw does the work.

#argument
1xrequired
2yrequired
3zrequired
4blockrequired

gfx.vterrain

gfx.vterrain(heights, top, sub, deep [, subdepth])

Extrude a w*d byte string of column heights (row-major) in ONE call. This is how a world gets built: Lua does the noise, C does the filling.

#argument
1heightsrequired
2toprequired
3subrequired
4deeprequired
5subdepthoptional, default 3

gfx.vworld

gfx.vworld{w=,d=,h=,chunk=} -> bool

engine v17

Allocate the block grid. One per app run; the world dies with the app. Cells are 1 byte, 0 = air, so 128x128x48 is 786KB of PSRAM where the same grid as a Lua table would blow the 2MB heap. w and d must be multiples of chunk.

#argument
1cfgrequired
4 table fields, with defaults
wdefault 64.0
ddefault 64.0
hdefault 32.0
chunkdefault 16.0
